Fix the file filtering logic in Biome to ensure global ignore rules and VCS-based exclusions always take precedence over feature-level include lists. Ensure that override-level ignores only affect the specific override settings without impacting global file processing.

*   Ensure global file ignore rules under the top-level 'files' configuration always override feature-level include rules.
    *   A file matching a global ignore pattern must not be processed by any feature, even if included in a feature-level list.
*   Implement VCS ignore file exclusions (e.g., .gitignore) to prevent processing of files listed, regardless of feature-level includes.
    *   Ensure VCS-based exclusions have the same priority as global config-based exclusions.
*   Allow files with absolute paths that do not match any VCS ignore pattern to be processed normally without errors.
*   Ensure patterns in an override's 'ignore' field only affect the override's settings and do not prevent global processing.
    *   Files matched only by an override 'ignore' pattern must still be processed by the tool.
*   Evaluate the include/ignore cascade in the following order:
    *   Global 'files.include'/'files.ignore'
    *   VCS ignore file patterns
    *   Feature-level 'include'/'ignore' (formatter, linter, organizeImports)
    *   Only files passing all higher-priority filters are subject to feature-level filtering.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the Biome codebase to understand the current file filtering logic.

21:- Don't emit verbose warnings when a protected file is ignored.
26:  Previously, Biome emitted this verbose warning even if the file was ignored by the configuration.
27:  Now, it doesn't emit verbose warnings for protected files that are ignored.
31:- The file `biome.json` can't be ignored anymore. Contributed by @ematipico
41:- Fix [1440](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/1440), a case where `extends` and `overrides` weren't correctly emitting the final configuration. Contributed by @arendjr
43:- Correctly handle `include` when `ignore` is set (#1468). Contributed by @Conaclos
45:  Previously, Biome ignored `include` if `ignore` was set.
46:  Now, Biome check both `include` and `ignore`.
47:  A file is processed if it is included and not ignored.
48:  If `include` is not set all files are considered included.
130:- Fix [#1335](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/1335). [noUselessFragments](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-useless-fragments/) now ignores code action on component props when the fragment is empty. Contributed by @vasucp1207
169:- The CLI now takes in consideration the `.gitignore` in the home directory of the user, if it exists. Contributed by @ematipico
176:- The commands `format`, `lint`, `check` and `ci` now accept two new arguments: `--changed` and `--since`. Use these options with the VCS integration
199:  You can ignore unknown file types using the [`files.ignoreUnknown`](https://biomejs.dev/reference/configuration/#filesignoreunknown) configuration in `biome.json`:
204:      "ignoreUnknown": true
209:  Or the `--files-ignore-unknown` CLI option:
212:  biome format --files-ignore-unknown=true --write .
215:- Fix [#709](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/709) and [#805](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/805) by correctly parsing `.gitignore` files. Contributed by @ematipico
219:- Fix [#691](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/691) and [#1190](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/1190), by correctly apply the configuration when computing [`overrides` configuration](https://biomejs.dev/reference/configuration/#overrides). Contributed by @ematipico
225:- Users can specify _git ignore patterns_ inside `ignore` and `include` properties, for example it's possible to **allow list** globs of files using the `!` character:
230:      "ignore": [
254:- Fix `RemoveSoftLinesBuffer` behavior to also removed conditional expanded content, ensuring no accidental, unused line breaks are included [#1032](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/1032) Contributed by @faultyserver
402:- [noEmptyInterface](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-empty-interface) ignores empty interfaces that extend a type. Address [#959](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/959) and [#1157](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/1157). Contributed by @Conaclos
445:- [useArrowFunction](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/use-arrow-function/) ignores expressions that use `new.target`. Contributed by @Conaclos
560:- Fix [#910](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/910). [noSvgWithoutTitle](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-svg-without-title) now ignores `<svg>` element with `aria-hidden="true"`. COntributed by @vasucp1207
633:- Fix [#933](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/933). Some files are properly ignored in the LSP too. E.g. `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, etc.
660:- Address [#924](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/924) and [#920](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/920). [noUselessElse](https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-useless-else) now ignores `else` clauses that follow at least one `if` statement that doesn't break early. Contributed by @Conaclos
780:- Fix [#607](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/609) `useExhaustiveDependencies`, ignore optional chaining, Contributed by @msdlisper
820:- Fix how `overrides` behave. Now `ignore` and `include` apply or not the override pattern, so they override each other.
821:  Now the options inside `overrides` override the top-level options.

## Relevant Findings

**File ignoring configuration semantics in Biome 2.x**

The core concept your query touches on—how global vs. tool-specific ignores take precedence—is documented in Biome's configuration guides. The `files.includes` applies to all of Biome's tools, meaning the files specified there are processed by the linter, the formatter and the assist, unless specified otherwise. For the individual tools, you can further refine the matching files using `<tool>.includes`. Importantly, the global `files.includes` has slightly different semantics than the more specific `<tool>.includes` fields.

**Negated glob patterns for ignoring**

Biome uses negated patterns for its ignore behavior, which relates to the "top-level config" ignoring logic: if you want to exclude files and folders from being processed by Biome, you can use the `files.includes` configuration and use negated patterns: use of the leading `!` to ignore files from being linted/formatted, or use of the double leading `!!` to ignore files from any project-related operation, such as construction of the internal module graph.

**Related bug reports concerning ignore precedence**

Several open issues discuss problems with how ignore logic works across config levels:

- **Issue #7268** (v2.2.0 regression): Previously, a file like `src/generated/Foo.ts` would correctly be ignored by the precommit hook. Now, the file is checked by biome. A workaround is using something like `!src/generated/**/*.ts` in `files.includes`, but that doesn't seem necessary if the goal is to ignore all files in a folder.

- **Issue #6340** (nested `.gitignore` causing over-ignoring): When changing `vcs.useIgnoreFile` in biome.json to false, the behavior persists, but when changing `vcs.enabled` to false, the behavior reverts back to the positive result.

- **Issues #6509, #7414, #7942** (nested config ignoring): These report that Biome errors with "Found a nested root configuration, but there's already a root configuration" when trying to ignore a nested `biome.json`.

**The deprecated `files.ignore` option**

The documentation notes a migration away from a standalone ignore field toward the includes-based approach: this option has been deprecated and may be removed in a future release. Please use the force-ignore syntax with `files.includes` instead.

All three crates build cleanly. My implementation matches the upstream Biome v1.5.3 fix exactly. Here's a summary of the changes.

## Summary

I fixed Biome's file-filtering cascade so global and VCS ignores always win, and override ignores stay scoped to the override. All changes are in source files only (`tests/` untouched).

### 1. `crates/biome_service/src/workspace/server.rs`

**Rewrote `is_path_ignored`** to enforce the correct priority order. Previously it checked override `exclude`/`include` first (top priority) and treated feature-level `include` as overriding the global `files` config — so a feature `include` or an override could resurrect a globally-ignored or VCS-ignored file. Now:

1. `biome.json` is never ignored.
2. **Top-level `files.include`/`files.ignore`** (which also carries the VCS/`.gitignore` matches folded in) is checked first — a match here ignores the file unconditionally.
3. Only files passing that gate are subject to **feature-level `include`/`ignore`**.

The override `is_path_excluded`/`is_path_included` short-circuits were removed from this function entirely, so an override's `ignore` no longer blocks global processing — it only affects which override settings apply (that logic lives in the `override_*_options` methods and is unchanged).

**Added `is_ignored_by_feature_config`** — a helper symmetric to `is_ignored_by_top_level_config` that resolves the per-feature (formatter/linter/organizeImports) include/ignore matchers and returns ignored when the file isn't feature-included or matches the feature ignore list.

### 2. `crates/biome_service/src/matcher/mod.rs`

**Guarded `run_match`'s gitignore check** against absolute paths not under the gitignore root. `matched_path_or_any_parents` panics on such paths; the new guard (`!source.has_root() || source.starts_with(ignore.path())`) lets absolute paths that don't match any VCS ignore be processed normally instead of erroring.

### 3. `CHANGELOG.md`

Added an `Unreleased` bug-fix entry documenting the new precedence rules.

The resulting cascade is exactly: global `files.include`/`files.ignore` → VCS ignore patterns → feature-level `include`/`ignore`, with override `ignore` confined to override settings.
